text.p: ValuJet Inc reaffirmed Wednesday it expects to report a "significant" loss in the first quarter, but expects to return to profitability by the third quarter.
"As we've told the world already, we expect a significant loss in the first quarter," said Stephen Nevin, ValuJet's chief financial officer.

"We may have some additional non-recurring costs after the first quarter, but the majority of this non-recurring stuff will be behind us soon," Nevin said, speaking at Dillon Read's Airlines, Aviation Services and Logistics Conference in Manhattan.

Nevin said the low-cost carrier expects to have 30 aircraft in service by the summer, up from the current level of 24 jets. ValuJet can maintain profitability with about 25-30 aircraft in operations, Nevin said.
"We're on the road to recovery, but it is paved with difficulty and it is slow going," Nevin said.
ValuJet's load factor has been increasing, with results for March expected to surpass February's load factor of 55.7 percent, Nevin said.
Atlanta-based ValuJet was allowed to resume a limited schedule in September after being grounded in June following the May 11 crash in the Florida Everglades that killed all 110 people on board.
The low-cost carrier has slowly been rebuilding its operations.
